title: Add benchmark-lab cold-start profiling baselines and reporting pipeline
author: Priya Nair
description: Summary: Add cold-start profiling baselines and extend the benchmark-lab reporting pipeline to ingest and visualize cold-start metrics; introduce representative workload runners that exercise cold-start scenarios for GPU-backed runtimes. Motivation: Production customers report significant tail latency on first requests after model/worker spin-up. We need reproducible baselines to measure regressions and guide optimizations (warm vs cold comparisons), and an automated reporting pipeline so daily/weekly baselines show up in the perf dashboards. What this PR does: (1) adds a new set of profiling baselines under benchmark-lab/profiling/cold_start that run a mix of short-sequence and long-sequence prompts across model families and quantization profiles; (2) introduces representative workload runners (cold_start_runner) that simulate realistic request patterns including prefix-skew and random inter-arrival gaps; (3) extends the reporting pipeline (pipeline/ingest/cold_start_reporter) to collect cold-start metrics (first-token latency, KV cache fill time, allocator spikes) and write them to the perf-store; (4) adds a nightly CI job benchmark-lab/cold-start to run a lightweight matrix on PRs and full baselines on main; (5) dashboard tiles and alerts for cold-start regression (>15% increase over 7-day baseline). Backwards compatibility: baselines are additive and opt-in; default workflows unchanged. Testing: unit tests for reporters, integration test that runs a simulated cold-start against the runtime docker image, and an end-to-end smoke run that uploads a sample report to a staging perf-store. Rollout plan: merge to main behind feature flag BENCH_COLD_START; enable nightly jobs gradually for internal staging then prod dashboards. Related: ENG-1124 tracks downstream infra work; ENG-1190 tracks follow-up optimizations in the serving runtime.
